> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **12** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/credential-literal.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-flow-template-paths.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-headers.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c5b43b606807e26d873e2407cbd38a844e624895` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c9e48bc488616eda62564208c8d7cf2d0763e008` — the merge of head `af1317fd10f1e1cb17d78931cf8a632e60724658` into base `c5b43b606807e26d873e2407cbd38a844e624895`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c9e48bc488616eda62564208c8d7cf2d0763e008 && git checkout c9e48bc488616eda62564208c8d7cf2d0763e008
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c5b43b606807e26d873e2407cbd38a844e624895 af1317fd10f1e1cb17d78931cf8a632e60724658 && git checkout -B drift-repro c5b43b606807e26d873e2407cbd38a844e624895 && git merge --no-ff af1317fd10f1e1cb17d78931cf8a632e60724658

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c5b43b606807e26d873e2407cbd38a844e624895
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c5b43b606807e26d873e2407cbd38a844e624895` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1105b4a069d6071f3947345639a583245d0332a3`
Local-runs: none

Read at 2026-10-12T15:03Z by the isolated at-tier reviewer of `domain:spec` seat 1 (#6017), on PR #23062 (`Part of #19939`, pass 4 stage S5). Head confirmed: `git rev-parse` of `1105b4a069` on the fetched branch equals the PR's `head.sha`; the net diff is against the merge base `9f4b652e3` (46 files, +1,528 / -346); the PR read `draft`, `mergeable_state` `blocked` at the first read and `unknown` at the second (a recompute after the red named below). Inputs: card #19939's body and all 63 comments (the stage plan `6096263424`, the S4 seat order `6117306001`, the claim `6122880753`, the dev report `6126394968`, the ACCEPT `6126438722` included), the PR body, file list and diff, and the head's check-runs read twice. Two spellings are written in words below because a double-brace opener in a comment is read as a stamp token: "double-brace hole" is the text-slot dialect of ADR-0032 Decision 3, "single-brace token" the retired 17.x dialect.

**Verdict in one line: the contract judgments ①②③ stand, and the head is refused on one count — a dependent pin in `packages/metadata-protocol` writes the retired single-brace spelling at an http `url` and header and expects the save door not to refuse it; this diff retires exactly that and did not re-judge the fixture, the census row that claims every test file missed it, and `Test Core (5/6)` is red on that package while the base is green. One fixture rewrite and a run over the dependents is the patch round.**

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, judged against the tree at the head and at the base (read with `git show` / `git grep`; nothing run):

1. **`url` and every `headers` value become text slots (double-brace holes); a single-brace token there is refused by the contract, at `registerFlow`, at `objectstack validate`, at the metadata save door and by the executor's parse.** Right. The stage plan's carry line binds it (`6096263424`: "that makes `notify.actionUrl`, `http.url` and `http.headers.*` text slots"). `HttpConfigSchema`'s `superRefine` composes the one text-slot judge (`textSlotTemplateRefusal`) at the url and per header value; `FLOW_NODE_TEXT_SLOTS` gains the two rows, the `headers` row flagged `eachValue`. Every non-test reader of that roster at the head goes through `flowNodeTextSlotSources` (lint `validate-expressions.ts:2492`, `lint-flow-patterns.ts:2047`, `engine.ts:10850`) or strips by key (`withoutTextSlots`), so the new map-valued row is judged at every door and skipped at none. The `$runId` the examples and the whole-map remedy write is in the engine's bound `$` roots (`flow-text-slot-template.ts:137`). Census of shipped surfaces: `git grep` at `9f4b652e3` finds no single-brace token at `url` or at any header in `examples/**`, `content/docs/**` (references and releases excluded), `docs/**`, `packages/qa` or `packages/platform-objects`.
2. **`body` becomes a value slot (`FlowValueSlotSchema`): a CEL envelope evaluated once before either mode, a literal sent as written, a single-brace token in any string of a literal refused, a malformed envelope refused.** Right. `FLOW_NODE_EXPRESSION_PATHS` gains the `http.body (value)` row with every older row pinned byte-identical; `HttpConfigSchema` joins `LEDGER_DECLARED_NODE_CONFIG_SCHEMAS`, so the marker reaches the reconciliation ratchet on one channel (the descriptor offers `body` with no marker, pinned in `config-expression-ledger.test.ts`). `celValueSlotSchema` is `z.unknown().superRefine(…)`, so the `HttpConfig` TS type of `body` stays `unknown` and the published JSON Schema stays `{}` plus the `xExpression: 'value'` marker and description — an annotation, not a wider accept set — while the runtime refuses more, which is exactly why `automation/HttpConfig` enters the dropped-refinements ledger at `""` and `body` (711 → 713). The executor's call `resolveValueSlot(engine, cfg.body, variables, 'body', context)` matches the signature at the head. Census: five tokens in four shipped bodies (showcase `flows/index.ts` at 1059, 1239, 1444; `flows.mdx` at 464), all migrated in this diff; `git grep` at the base finds the same bodies. A CEL map literal that mixes a literal with a field read needs `dyn(…)`; the examples, the describe, the docs and the changeset write it.
3. **`method`, `durable`, `timeoutMs` and `signingSecret` are literals read as written; a single-brace token or a CEL envelope there is refused with the literal's remedy.** Right under S4's answer B (`6117306001`) applied per key: zero shipped tokens at all four at the base (corroborated by `git grep`), the only sites being tests that pinned the interpolation itself, each re-judged in this diff. The refusals at `method`, `durable`, `timeoutMs` and at a token written as the whole `headers` map carry `READ_AS_WRITTEN_PARAM`, so the build doors' value arm reports them as the run would (S4's mechanism, unchanged). The refinement runs with a `when` that is always true, so a typed literal's token draws the type's refusal beside the remedy at the executor and the doors report the marked one — pinned (`['custom', 'invalid_type']`).
4. **`signingSecret`: the credential channel and `RUN_RESOLVED_KEYS` are byte-identical; the token refusal is the executor's parse alone and never echoes the value.** Right — the order is judged in ③. Confirmed at the head: `FLOW_CREDENTIAL_CLEARED` is `''`, so a cleared secret never reads as a token; a held store row replaces the authored value before the parse (`http-nodes.ts`, the credential channel); `parseNodeConfig` renders `path: message` and no input (`parse-config.ts:103`), and `HTTP_SIGNING_SECRET_TOKEN_REFUSAL` names no value. The 17.x "set but resolved to no value" refusal goes with the interpolation it guarded.
5. **The executor parses as authored after the credential channel, renders the url and headers and evaluates the body once before either mode, and no longer imports `interpolate`; `PARSED_AFTER_INTERPOLATION` and its line in `builtinValueJudged` are deleted.** Right: the set had one member and would be a check that can never fire; the durable enqueue is pinned to carry the rendered url, headers and payload with nothing left to render at delivery. The three `??` that remain are the documented absent-key defaults (`method` per mode, `payload`), not tolerance of an off-spec shape, so Prime Directive #12 holds.
6. **A header that renders to no text is not sent (17.x sent it empty); a url that renders to no text refuses the node.** Right and declared: pinned in `http-slots.test.ts`, stated in the changeset's FROM → TO table and in the text-slot D3 entry's acceptance criteria.
7. **Public surface.** The diff adds or removes no `export` in any package (checked over the whole diff), and the `api-surface/` snapshot is rightly untouched. `FlowNodeTextSlot (interface)`, `HttpConfigSchema (const)` and `LEDGER_DECLARED_NODE_CONFIG_SCHEMAS (const)` are published (`api-surface/automation.json`), so the two widenings the Clause-② line names — the optional `eachValue` member and the `http` key — are real published-surface changes. The pinned objectui sibling (`9646e2ed2b`) reads `LEDGER_DECLARED_NODE_CONFIG_SCHEMAS` only through a union and a lookup (`flow-node-config.contractKeys-11968.test.tsx`), never a pinned key set, and reads neither `FLOW_NODE_TEXT_SLOTS` nor `FlowNodeTextSlot`: nothing is removed and nothing the sibling imports moves; the Console Pin Gate's `skipped` on this head is its paths filter (the pin did not move), not a missing reading.
8. **ADR-0087: D3 only, no D2, no tombstone.** Right: no key is removed; the four step-18 entries are amended in the diff; the no-D2 reasons (a Date JSON-quoted vs ISO text; an absent value writing `null` or nothing vs a CEL fault; a whole token at a typed key resolving to its type vs text) are the reasons the earlier text-slot and value-slot stages recorded.
9. **Generated artifacts.** The `.describe()` restatements regenerate `content/docs/references/automation/io-node-config.mdx` (in the diff); `json-schema.manifest/` lists schema names, not contents, so it is rightly unmoved; the authorable key set of `HttpConfig` is unchanged; `Type Check · consumer gates` (`check:docs`, `check:api-surface`, `check:exported-any`) and the aggregate `TypeScript Type Check` are success on the head.
10. **Lint.** `NOTIFY_LITERAL_*` become the per-node-type `LITERAL_KEYS` / `LITERAL_HINTS` (non-exported); the http literal set is pinned against the contract ("asked of the contract, never listed"); `objectstack validate` refuses each position through the shared judges and the contract with no rule change. Right.
11. **The retired spelling's sites in the repository's tests — WRONG in one row, and the one count this head is refused on.** The PR's census claims every test file and lists, for `url`, four sites and, for `headers.*`, two plus the lint's credential-literal fixtures; the PR body says "test fixtures that wrote the retired spellings at these keys are re-judged". `packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.flow-credential-literal.test.ts` is missing from that row: its DARK case (line 39, `url: 'https://example.invalid/hook?api_key={api_token}'`; line 42, `Authorization: 'Bearer {api_token}'`) saves an active flow through `evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate` and asserts `verdict.error` is null — "the publish is NOT refused". On this head that pin cannot pass, by construction, not by flakiness: the gate runs `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` (`@objectstack/lint/runtime`), whose `EXPRESSION_INVALID` rule runs for a `flow` write (`authoring-rules.ts:684–686`, `runStackExpressionPasses`), and that pass now refuses a single-brace token at an http url and at each header value at `error` through the text-slot judge — the diff's own `validate-expressions.test.ts` pins exactly that — and an `error` finding is the gate's refusal (`runtime-authoring-gate.ts`, "errors refuse, warnings advise"). The diff rewrote the same two controls in the lint's own `lint-flow-credential-literals.test.ts` to double-brace holes and left this sibling, in a package the diff does not touch but which depends on `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/lint`; the dev report's `tests` field lists spec, service-automation, lint and the showcase, no dependent, so the closure `turbo ls --affected` names was not run. The red is at the SAVE door, a door this stage claims. Remedy, mechanical: rewrite the DARK fixture's `url` and `Authorization` to the double-brace spelling (the connector input's `clientSecret: '{api_token}'` is not an http position and stays), run the affected closure (or `pnpm test`, Post-Task Checklist 1), and correct the census row and the "re-judged" sentence in the PR body. No contract text changes.

Wrong: item 11. Items 1–10 stand and carry to the next head's record unchanged unless the patch round moves them.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/19939-flow-http-slots.md`: `@objectstack/spec` **major**, `@objectstack/service-automation` **major**, `@objectstack/lint` **patch** — matches what the diff publishes: an accept-set narrowing on a published authoring contract (`HttpConfigSchema`) and on the executor (a template secret, a token at any key and a malformed envelope now refused; a header that renders empty omitted), on the v18 line (`.changeset/pre.json` is `mode: pre`, `tag: next` at the base); the lint ships hint text and a per-node literal map only, its refusals coming from the spec. The levels equal stages S3 (`19939-flow-collection-value-slots.md`) and S4 (`19939-flow-notify-value-slots.md`) at the base. No `skip-changeset` label, rightly.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing: …; widening: …)`: the arm word is the first token in the parenthetical, so `clause2-line.mjs` reads `yes` with the `narrowing` arm — breaking, `major` — the shape S2 ruled and S3/S4 wrote. The `yes` is true on the published `FlowNodeTextSlot` member and the `LEDGER_DECLARED_NODE_CONFIG_SCHEMAS` key; the third item it names (the JSON Schema `body` marker) is an annotation on an unchanged `{}` schema rather than a wider accept set — a wording nit that moves neither the arm nor the level. The same line sits in the PR body and in the changeset body, where `check-adr-0087-registration` reads it.
- ADR-0087 marker: `not-required (already-registered …)` naming the four step-18 ids, each amended in this diff, with the no-D2 reasons stated; no key removed, so no tombstone. The breaking changeset carries its FROM → TO table and the one-line fix (Post-Task Checklist 3). `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are success on the head.
- Comment-only touches in `@objectstack/service-messaging` (a TSDoc on `HttpDelivery.headers`) and `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks` (`webhook-headers.ts`) publish no behaviour or surface and owe no changeset entry; `examples/app-showcase` is private. The patch round's fixture edit publishes nothing and changes none of this.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report `6126394968`: `open_questions` is empty. Every `out_of_scope_findings` entry, every `deviations` entry and the PR's Acceptance notes, answered:

- **The `signingSecret` order — the token refused only at the executor's parse.** Judged RIGHT and not escalated; the maintainer's veto window stands as it did for S4's answer B. The binding text keeps the key's run-resolved resolution exactly as it is and forbids a template or value slot there: the resolution that stays is the write-only credential channel (`holdsFlowCredential` / `resolveFlowCredential`, `RUN_RESOLVED_KEYS`), all byte-identical, and the only other reading — keeping the single-brace interpolator alive on this one key — contradicts the dispatch's own A3 (the executor no longer calls `interpolate`) and S7's resolver deletion. Leaving the key to the run is the pre-existing #21898 carve-out, not a new choice: the build doors did not judge this key at 17.x either, so no door regresses, and the one accept-set change is at the run and fail-closed (a guard, nothing sent, `config.signingSecret` named, the remedy naming the secret itself or `''`, no value echoed) — louder than 17.x, where a token resolving to nothing was also caught only at the run. The residual the dev names is real and bounded: a Studio save of a single-brace token at this key is accepted into the credential store and every run of that node refuses, loudly; refusing at the save door would mean reading the marked refusal ahead of `RUN_RESOLVED_KEYS` and would also refuse a packaged flow whose store row supplies the real secret — a contract decision outside this stage, correctly left in the Acceptance notes for the seat. A follow-up the seat may take without touching the run-resolved order: a `warn`-level lint hint at that key.
- **Skill text `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md:236–241` lists `http` among the single-brace slots.** Right not to touch: `skills/**` is Tier H and one path would make this PR Tier H; the stage plan assigns the pointer to #22585 at each landing. Carried by the seat.
- **objectui designer: the `url` picker writes single-brace tokens; `body` is stored as a JSON string.** Carried to the objectui companion per the stage plan (objectui#12101 is the route the ACCEPT names). For the carry: a JSON-string body was already broken silently at the 17.x run (the interpolator read it as a token); it is loud at save now, the right direction. Not a Console Pin Gate matter (nothing the sibling imports moves; ① 7).
- **A CEL map literal needs `dyn(…)`.** A property of the CEL checker, refused loudly at `registerFlow` with the value-slot remedy naming `dyn(…)`; the examples, describe, docs and changeset write it. No action.
- **hotcrm NOT MEASURED at the http keys.** Another repository; it joins the existing hotcrm carry on this card (stage plan: recorded on seat post #18549's ledger). No action here.
- **Files beyond the claim's surface.** Each is named in the PR body with its reason, and each is a mechanical consequence of the slots or a stale sentence about them (the ledger body row, the ledger-declared map, the dropped-refinements ledger, the builtin-values D3 entry and its `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment, docblocks, two comment-only sibling-package edits, test fixtures). Accepted. The patch round adds one more file of the same class, in `packages/metadata-protocol`, and the PR body names it the same way.
- **In-place fixes under the exemption** (`template.ts` and `flows.mdx` still called a notify recipient single-brace; the README named `recipients`; a ledger test comment counted S4's notify rows as six). Read in the diff: the same stale single-brace teaching S4 retired, mechanical, same gate family. Accepted.
- **Two sentences at the executor for a token at a typed literal** (a `when` that is always true). The doors report the marked one, once; the executor's refusal naming both the type and the remedy is loud, not wrong. Accepted; pinned.
- **A header that renders to no text is omitted.** Declared in the changeset and the D3 entry; pinned. Accepted (① 6).
- **PR-context guards run locally while the body says CI's runs are the record.** CI's three guard check-runs are success on the head. Resolved.
